newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrials end weak, minings unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrials end weak, minings unchanged.

text.p: Zimbabwe industrial shares met up to expectations on Friday and closed weaker, while the mining index finished the day unchanged.
Dealers said that Thursday's negative sentiment had survived overnight and infiltrated the market again, weighing it down despite reasonable levels of turnover.
"Yesterday we thought it would continue weak today and it did. No surprises, but hopefully next week might see some recovery," one dealer said.
"Industrials enjoyed quite a bit of activity and the minings that traded had fair volumes," he added.
Dealers said that pretty soon bargains would begin to surface and bargain-hunting would start buoying the industrial index.
The 57-counter industrial index lost 31.2 points to 10,132.96, while the mining index finished unchanged from Thursday at 970.35 points -- just off a 29-month low.
Ashanti, Bindurc, Falgold and Wankie WNKI.J were unchanged although the latter two enjoyed reasonable turnover.
Hippo cut 50 cents to 1,450, Bicaf lost 20 cents to 400, Colcom shed 25 cents to 470 and TA Prefs was 100 down at 4,500.
